vedha
(‘intermixed’)
------------------------------------------
Vedha (‘pierced’ or ‘intermixed’) is a technical term used in Hindu pañcāṅgas or almanacs. It belongs to the field of ज्यौतिष or अस्त्रोनोम्य्.
According to the cāndramāna or lunar चलेन्दर्, a day (from sunrise to the next sunrise) is divided into 60 ghaṭikās (1 ghaṭikā = 24 minutes). If a tithi (like pratipad, dvitīyā and so on, the number of the day after new-मोओन् or full-मोओन्) is spread over all the 60 ghaṭikās, it is called pūrṇā. If another tithi begins some time after sunrise or before sunset, the tithi becomes viddhā or with वेध. For instance, the tithi at sunrise on a day may be tṛtīyā (3rd) and caturthi (4th) may begin after six ghaṭikās. Then it is viddha-tithi.
All religious rites including the vratas (vows and festivals) have to be started at the prescribed time even though the tithi may have वेध.
